We're growing fast and hiring the Engineering talent to match.

The team and the mission

You'd be joining our backend team within the Platform Engineering division.

We're building an AI-native platform for our internal developers, over 150 of them, guided by a single question: does this shorten the time from idea to value, for the teams building on our platform and for the customers they ultimately serve?

The smooth path is the safe, fast path, because the platform makes it the default. We build the route that maximizes AI acceleration.

You'll set the technical direction for how backend services get built, shipped, and operated across the engineering org — not just for one team.

What you’ll do:

 - Shape the technical direction, governance and architecture of the backend platform

 - Shape AI-native workflows into the platform itself, changing how the org builds services with developers and agents

 - Proactively identify and drive resolution of cross-cutting technical challenges before they become delivery blockers, working across multiple engineering teams

 - Define and evolve platform-wide standards, patterns, and abstractions adopted across teams

 - Influence roadmap priorities by framing trade-offs, surfacing opportunities, and driving alignment across engineering, product, and analytics

 - Drive adoption of changes across teams, not just their delivery

 - Mentor and elevate senior engineers through complex problems and architectural decisions

 - Navigate ambiguity and lead complex, multi-squad initiatives with minimal direction

 - Participate in the on-call rotation

About you:

 - A strong AI-native mindset — you've brought AI-assisted workflows into a platform or org, not just your own workflow.

 - Deep expertise in distributed systems, demonstrated with experience making architectural decisions with long-term, cross-org, multi-year consequences

 - Deep exposure across several of the platform's key domains: cloud (AWS), IaC infrastructure (Terraform/Atmos), CI/CD, GraphQL federation, Event driven systems, APIs, and developer experience

 - Expert in Node.js, TypeScript, or similar languages, with a track record of setting standards others adopt.

 - Track record of cross-team impact: changing how multiple teams build, decide, or deliver

 - Demonstrated ability to frame ambiguous technical problems and drive them to resolution with minimal guidance

 - Experience navigating organizational complexity, aligning stakeholders and using data to demonstrate impact

 - Strong technical judgment balanced with pragmatism: knows when to advocate for the right solution and when to move forward

 - Expert-level English, spoken and written — you'll lead platform engineering managers across multiple teams and present technical priorities to executive stakeholders.

 We are seeking an accomplished Senior Geotechnical Engineer – Tailings & Mine Waste to join our growing Tailings & Mine Waste team .  Our team delivers engineering and consulting services for tailings storage facilities, mine-waste facilities, waste rock facilities, and related mining infrastructure, supporting clients through investigation, design, construction, operation, monitoring, and closure. This is an opportunity to contribute to complex projects while working alongside experienced engineers and multidisciplinary teams.
 Why Join Equilibrium? 
 Global reach. Specialist expertise. Real influence. 
 The Role: 
 As a Senior Geotechnical Engineer, Tailings & Mine Waste , you’ll deliver complex tailings and mine waste projects, provide technical guidance, and work closely with clients and multidisciplinary teams. You’ll have the opportunity to apply your technical expertise across investigations, design, and facility assessments, mentor developing engineers, and contribute to the continued growth of Equilibrium’s Mine Waste practice.
 You will:
 Deliver Technical Projects: Manage geotechnical investigations, assessments, and designs for tailings, waste rock spoils and other mine waste facilities, confirming safe work practices, schedule, budget, and client requirements are met.
 Perform Technical Analysis: Perform, oversee, and review geotechnical analyses, interpret field and monitoring data, develop geotechnical models, and provide practical, risk-informed engineering recommendations.
 Support Field Activities: Plan and coordinate geotechnical investigations, inspections, and construction support activities, providing safety oversight, technical direction and responding to site conditions and emerging project requirements.
 Provide Technical Review: Prepare and review engineering reports, calculations, specifications, and technical documentation, while supporting technical reviews, dam safety assessments, risk evaluations, and quality assurance and quality control.
 Support Clients & Project Delivery: Serve as a point of contact for assigned scopes, communicate project status, technical findings and recommendations, and contribute to project planning, proposals, schedules, budgets, and client meetings.
 Develop People: Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and review to junior engineers, engineers-in-training, technologists, and field staff, supporting their professional development.

 What We’re Looking For: 
 7 - 10 years of relevant experience in geotechnical engineering, mining, engineering consulting, mine waste, tailings, or project delivery.
 Demonstrated experience in geotechnical design and evaluation of tailings dams, waste rock spoils, and/or co-management structures.
 Demonstrated commitment to health and safety, with experience identifying and managing risks in mine site, field, and project environments. Dam Safety experience considered an asset.
 Strong technical judgement, leadership and project coordination skills.
 Strong interpersonal and emotional intelligence, with the ability to communicate thoughtfully, build trust, provide constructive technical feedback, and navigate challenging situations with empathy.
 Experience contributing to business development, cross-selling, and building long-term client relationships.
 Willingness to travel to mine sites as required.
 Education & Certifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Geological, or related discipline).
 Professional Engineering designation (P.Eng.) or equivalent professional registration required where applicable.

 Complex challenges. Practical solutions. Technical excellence.

 Different perspectives make us stronger.

 $120,000 to $145,000 CAD per year + Benefits + Bonus

In addition, this role is also responsible for the universities energy management programs and storm water management systems across the campus.  This includes ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of campus utilities while advancing energy conservation initiatives that support the University’s sustainability goals.
 The Director leads the planning and management of utility infrastructure operations, supports long-term renewal planning for energy systems, and works collaboratively across Facilities and campus partners to optimize energy performance and system reliability.
 University of Waterloo infrastructure supports more than eight million square feet of academic, research, and administrative space across multiple campuses. The associated energy systems are critical to maintaining safe and effective teaching, research, and campus operations. The Director works in close partnership with the Chief Stationary Engineer to ensure that energy and utility systems are planned, resourced, and operated in alignment with institutional priorities, regulatory requirements, and long‑term infrastructure strategies.
 This role contributes to the Plant Operations goal of providing a safe, reliable, accessible, and well-maintained campus environment through service excellence, operational efficiency, and responsible stewardship of energy resources.
 Key Accountabilities 
 Strategic Planning 
 Acts as the subject matter expert and ensures implementation of the Deferred Capital Renewal plan for energy utility and building systems, ensuring alignment with the University’s long-term academic, research, and campus growth objectives.
 Establishes long-term strategies for the capacity, reliability, and resilience of campus energy infrastructure, including district energy systems, electrical distribution, and utility supply.
 Identifies and prioritizes infrastructure renewal and modernization initiatives related to energy and core building systems to mitigate risks associated with aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance.
 Provides strategic advice to the Executive Director, Facilities and senior leadership regarding long-term utility infrastructure requirements, emerging technologies, and infrastructure risks.
 Directs the development of long-range infrastructure investment plans, balancing operational needs, sustainability commitments, and available funding.
 Develops performance indicators and analytical frameworks to support data-driven decision-making related to infrastructure performance, asset lifecycle management, and system reliability.
 Monitors external trends including energy markets, regulatory changes, and technological advancements and assesses their potential impact on campus infrastructure planning.
 Works collaboratively with the Chief Stationary Engineer to align utility and energy infrastructure planning, performance objectives, and renewal priorities within Central Plants operating capabilities and constraints.
 Partners with the Chief Stationary Engineer to assess operational risks, system reliability trends, and capacity limitations, and to develop mitigation and investment strategies.
 Energy Management 
 Leads the University of Waterloo’s Energy Management program, identifying and implementing initiatives to improve energy efficiency and reduce institutional energy consumption.
 Works collaboratively with the Sustainability Office and campus partners to support the University’s sustainability goals.
 Provides technical expertise to the Executive Director, Facilities on matters related to energy consumption, utility supply, sustainability initiatives, and energy efficiency opportunities.
 Oversees development of multi-year utility forecasts, incorporating projected consumption, regulatory changes, and energy market conditions.
 Directs the evaluation of campus energy systems to identify energy conservation opportunities and operational improvements.
 Oversees the development of business cases, funding proposals, and external submissions related to energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives.
 Provides oversight to the Energy Manager in the negotiation and management of utility supply contracts and agreements.
 Collaborates with faculty, staff, and students on the implementation of energy reduction initiatives, ensuring alignment with the University’s academic and research mission.
 Infrastructure Renewal 
 Contributes to capital planning and infrastructure renewal planning related to energy, utility and building systems.

Built on a native, AI-powered platform and more than a decade of proprietary data—including billions of social interactions, impressions, and $2.4B+ in verified influencer-driven purchases—Later helps teams understand what will work before they launch.
 Senior MLOps Engineer 
 Later is the world’s most intelligent influencer marketing company. Built on a native, AI-powered platform and more than a decade of proprietary data, including billions of social interactions and $2.4B+ in verified influencer-driven purchases, Later helps brands choose the right creators, run fully managed campaigns, and know what will work before they launch.
 Trusted by leading enterprise brands including Nike, Wayfair, Unilever, and Southwest Airlines, Later bridges creativity and performance so campaigns don’t just look good, they deliver results. Learn more at later.com.
 About this position 
 We’re looking for a Senior MLOps Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure that takes Later’s machine learning and AI systems from prototype to production. You’ll own the pipelines that train, retrain, deploy, and serve the models behind our products, including forecasting, recommendation, and LLM-based and agentic features, across AWS and GCP.
 You’ll join the Infrastructure team alongside our DevOps engineers and work closely with Data Science, Data Engineering, Platform, and Product Engineering. Data Science builds and iterates on models; you make sure they ship reliably, scale with demand, and retrain on the right cadence.
 At first, expect roughly half your time on ML platform work and half on shared infrastructure. The split will shift toward ML as the practice grows into its own team. The role is mainly infrastructure and automation, with hands-on coding where it counts.
 This is a strong fit for a senior engineer with a solid DevOps and cloud foundation and real experience putting ML systems into production, who wants to set the standard for MLOps at Later.
 What you’ll be doing 
 Strategy & Architecture 
 Own the MLOps roadmap with Infrastructure, Data Science, and Data Engineering leaders, aligned to product and AI growth plans.
 Evaluate and select tooling for orchestration, model registry, experiment tracking, LLM serving, and observability, and make clear build-or-buy recommendations.
 Shape the long-term architecture of our multi-cloud ML and data platform, with scalability, security, and cost built in from the start.
 Building & Operating 
 Design, build, and operate infrastructure that deploys and scales ML models in production, using CI/CD, GitOps, Kubernetes, and orchestration tools such as Airflow, Kubeflow, or Argo Workflows.
 Own automated training and retraining pipelines, including model registry, validation, deployment, and rollback, and agree on the retraining cadence with Data Science.
 Deploy and operate LLM inference (self-hosted on AWS Bedrock or managed APIs), including GPU capacity, cost controls, and performance monitoring.
 Manage training and inference infrastructure across AWS and GCP, including GPU workloads, using Terraform.
 Work with Data Engineering to source and prepare training data from BigQuery and S3, building pipelines and light transformations as needed.
 Build monitoring for model performance, latency, data drift, cost, and resource usage, using tools such as CloudWatch, Prometheus, and Grafana.
 Support model versioning, experiment tracking (e.g., MLflow, SageMaker), and reproducible training workflows.
 Lead troubleshooting of complex production and deployment issues, and take part in the Infrastructure on-call rotation.
 Leadership & Collaboration 
 Set and document standards for infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, observability, secure deployment, and ML workflow automation.
 Write runbooks and self-serve guides so Product and Data teams can deploy, monitor, and troubleshoot with more autonomy.
 Lead incident reviews and post-mortems that improve how we operate.
 Mentor engineers through pairing, code review, and feedback.
 Explain technical tradeoffs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
 What success looks like 
 First 30 days: Learn and support. 
 You learn Later’s cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes environments, CI/CD workflows, and the data and ML platform, including how models are trained and deployed today. You start supporting existing pipelines and observability tools. By day 30 you know where the platform’s biggest gaps are and how Product and Data teams use it.
 First 60 days: Contribute and improve. 
 You own infrastructure and automation work across Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, and the ML platform. You make deployment pipelines more consistent and automated, improve GPU provisioning and monitoring for training and inference, and close gaps in alerting and runbooks. You’re already mentoring teammates on the patterns you’re introducing.
 First 90 days: Own and scale. 
 You own the path from a finished model to production. By day 90:
 At least one production model is deployed, retrained, and rolled back through an automated pipeline, with no manual steps.
 Drift, latency, and cost alerts are live for production models.
 A first MLOps roadmap has been reviewed with Infrastructure, Data Science, and Data Engineering leads.
 Security and compliance checks are built into the ML deployment path.
 What you bring 
 7+ years of DevOps, cloud, or software engineering experience in production environments, including technical leadership: leading projects, setting direction, and mentoring others. People management is not required.
 Deep expertise with Kubernetes (EKS), Helm, and microservices, including running GPU workloads on Kubernetes.
 Hands-on AWS experience and a track record of using Terraform for scalable, auditable infrastructure as code.
 Experience deploying, serving, and scaling ML models in production, including CI/CD for ML.
 Experience building data and training pipelines in partnership with Data Science and Data Engineering teams.
 Strong system design skills, including designing ML systems end to end and explaining the tradeoffs.
 Clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences.
 Nice to have 
 GCP experience, especially BigQuery.
 Amazon SageMaker.
 Self-hosted LLM deployments on Kubernetes (e.g., vLLM, KServe).
 Orchestration and experiment tracking tools such as Airflow, Kubeflow, Argo Workflows, or MLflow.
 If you don’t meet every requirement but this role sounds like you, we’d still love to hear from you.

 En près de 100 ans, nous avons réalisé de nombreuses percées dans le développement de moteurs qui assurent le transport de marchandises et de matériel, luttent contre les feux de forêt et effectuent le transport de passagers. 
 Un employeur de choix 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l'un des 10 meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2025 selon Forbes , en plus d’être classé au premier rang des employeurs dans l'industrie de l'aérospatiale et de la défense au pays! Notre siège social figure sur le palmarès des meilleurs employeurs dans la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d'employeur de choix dans la région de Montréal, au Canada et dans le monde. 
 À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien? 
 Travailler à partir d'instructions, de fiches de demandes de service et de processus établis, pour l'entretien préventif, prédictif, correctif, et tout genre de travaux de réparation mécanique sur divers équipements ou machineries. 
 Installer et assembler des équipements selon les besoins opérationnels. 
 Proposer et effectuer des modifications pour une mise à niveau des divers équipements et machineries. 
 Effectuer un diagnostic pour identifier la source du problème, démonter les équipements jusqu'aux pièces défectueuses et en maintient l’intégrité. 
 Rechercher la cause répétitive des pannes ou des bris et recommande les méthodes correctives efficaces. 
 Déterminer l’emplacement et l’agencement du matériel. 
 Estimer l'étendue des tâches et le matériel requis pour effectuer les réparations ou remplacements et organise son travail en collaboration avec les autres métiers. 
 Installer, remplacer, réparer, ajuster et aligner les pièces de divers équipements et machineries tel que; machines-outils, outils pneumatiques, pompes, soufflantes, armature et composantes externes de système de ventilation et filtration sur les machines. 
 Utiliser différents types de soudure, règle et conduit différent types de machines-outils pour fabriquer des pièces d'équipements. 
 Procéder aux essais des appareils et s'assure de leur rendement selon leurs spécifications et besoins opérationnels. 
 Effectuer l’entretien, réparer, modifier, installer, essayer et diagnostiquer les problèmes mécaniques des machines à contrôle numérique et autres équipements. 
 Utiliser les outils et appareillages appropriés afin de vérifier les paramètres, l’ajustement et le calibrage pour en assurer le bon fonctionnement. 
 Identifier, rechercher et préparer la commande ou l’expédition de pièces de rechange, de kits prêt-à-monter et de composantes réparables nécessaires à l’exécution des travaux. 
 Recevoir, déplacer du matériel, des pièces, et autres équipements aux endroits désignés. 
 Conduire divers équipements mobiles et véhicule motorisé tels que chariot élévateur et plate-forme de travail. 
 S'assurer de sécuriser de façon appropriée son périmètre de travail en plus d'effectuer le cadenassage d’équipement selon les procédures en place.

 Titulaire d’un DEP en mécanique industriel 
 Expertise en équipement d’analyse prédictive et suivi de conditions machine 
 Habileté marquée en résolution de problèmes et d’esprit d’analyse 
 Maitrise de la lecture de plans mécanique, hydraulique et pneumatique 
 Capacités interpersonnelles : travail d’équipe et attitude positive 
 Familiarité avec les systèmes informatiques, système d’exploitation Windows et la suite Microsoft 
 Bonnes habiletés manuelles et bonne dextérité manuelle 
 Bonne acuité visuelle et auditive 
 Rigueur, minutie, précision et souci du détail 
 Sens de l’observation et de l’initiative. 
 Capacité de s’adapter aux nombreux changements technologiques 
 Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une connaissance de base de l’anglais pour comprendre certaines instructions de travail spécialisées, des dessins et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales. 
 Ce que nous offrons 
 Programme d’assurance collective 
 Possibilités d’avancement (progression de carrière) 
 Programme de mérite ou programme de reconnaissance 
 Club récréatif et sportif 
 Garderies à proximité 
 Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, nous allions passion, audace et rigueur pour concevoir, fabriquer et entretenir les moteurs d’aéronefs les plus avancés et les plus fiables au monde. Notre travail et la qualité de nos produits contribuent au succès de nos clients, qui à leur tour sauvent des vies, soutiennent le commerce connectent les communautés et protègent les libertés.

The Opportunity: 
 Mattel is currently seeking a Manager, Quality Engineering. This role is a member of the corporate Quality Engineering team and is responsible for leading a team of Quality Engineers supporting Mattel Global Brand Teams and product development programs. The Manager will work directly with Marketing, Design, Product Development, other R&D support teams, Quality Data Analytics, Product Safety and Regulatory Compliance, laboratories, and global Manufacturing and Quality teams.
 The Manager, Quality Engineering will provide both people and technical leadership to ensure quality, safety, regulatory compliance, reliability, and consumer expectations are effectively integrated throughout the product development lifecycle. The Manager will shape and execute quality strategies within assigned brands, product categories, or areas of responsibility while developing engineering talent and driving consistent execution of Quality Engineering practices.
 The Manager will have responsibility for team performance, talent development, resource planning, technical execution, and quality outcomes within their assigned scope. This role requires strong technical judgment and the ability to influence cross-functional decisions while building a high-performing Quality Engineering team.
 What Your Impact Will Be: 
 Strategy Development & Execution 
 Shapes and executes Quality Engineering strategies within assigned brands, product categories, or functional areas to support business objectives and consumer expectations.
 Ensures consistent execution of product quality, safety, risk management, reliability, and regulatory requirements throughout the product development lifecycle.
 Maintains a strong understanding of applicable global toy and consumer product regulations, standards, and industry best practices and ensures requirements are effectively understood and implemented by the team.
 Maintains awareness of new and evolving regulatory requirements, standards, technologies, and industry practices and supports implementation of applicable changes within the organization.
 Identifies systemic product and process risks within assigned areas and develops strategies with appropriate cross-functional partners to mitigate those risks.
 Contributes Quality Engineering expertise and lessons learned to the development and improvement of broader organizational practices and processes.
 Leadership & Team Development 
 Leads, coaches, and develops a team of Quality Engineers, building capability in quality systems, regulatory requirements, technical problem-solving, risk management, data analysis, and decision-making.
 Establishes clear goals, priorities, expectations, and accountability for the team and ensures alignment with Quality Engineering and business objectives.
 Provides ongoing coaching, feedback, performance management, and career development for team members.
 Develops technical and leadership capability within the team through mentoring, stretch assignments, knowledge sharing, and development planning.
 Assesses team capability and resource needs and appropriately allocates engineering resources based on product complexity, risk, workload, and business priorities.
 Supports hiring, onboarding, development, succession planning, and retention of Quality Engineering talent.
 Creates an environment that encourages technical curiosity, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and appropriate escalation of product quality and safety concerns.
 Cross-Functional Influence 
 Builds strong partnerships with Marketing, Design, Product Development, Product Safety, Regulatory Compliance, Quality Data Analytics, Play Labs, Manufacturing, laboratories, and other cross-functional organizations.
 Ensures Quality Engineering is appropriately engaged throughout product development to influence decisions affecting product quality, safety, compliance, reliability, and consumer satisfaction.
 Anticipates downstream impacts, opportunities, and risks and ensures appropriate cross-functional engagement and communication for effective resolution.
 Influences cross-functional teams and leaders to make balanced, risk-based decisions while maintaining consumer safety and regulatory compliance as fundamental requirements.
 Provides Quality Engineering leadership during significant product quality, safety, compliance, manufacturing, and post-market issues.
 Establishes effective communication and escalation practices within the team to ensure significant risks are appropriately communicated to Quality Engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
 Decision-Making & Data Strategy 
 Promotes objective, data-driven decision-making throughout the Quality Engineering team.
 Ensures engineers identify, collect, analyze, and appropriately interpret data needed to support product quality and risk decisions.
 Reviews technical analyses and recommendations for complex or higher-risk issues and ensures conclusions are technically sound, clearly communicated, and appropriately documented.
 Utilizes product testing, consumer complaints, returns, Quality Data Analytics, Play Lab findings, manufacturing performance, and other available data to identify trends, emerging risks, and improvement opportunities.
 Establishes and monitors appropriate KPIs and quality metrics for assigned areas and ensures meaningful trends and issues result in appropriate action.
 Communicates significant quality trends, risks, and recommendations to Quality Engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
 Technical & Engineering Excellence 
 Provides technical leadership and oversight for product investigations, root cause analysis, engineering studies, sampling strategies, risk assessments, product verification, and validation activities.
 Ensures appropriate use of investigation and problem-solving methodologies such as Fishbone diagrams, 5-Why, FMEA, and other applicable root cause analysis tools.
 Provides oversight and guidance for the development and maintenance of Product Requirement Documents (PRDs), Primary Concerns Documents (PCDs), testing strategies, and other Quality Engineering documentation.
 Ensures product concepts, intended play patterns, foreseeable use and misuse, consumer interactions, and identified product risks are appropriately translated into robust testing and verification strategies.
 Partners with internal laboratories and third-party testing organizations to ensure testing strategies appropriately address regulatory requirements, identified risks, and product performance expectations.
 Ensures investigations and corrective actions are thorough, technically sound, appropriately documented, and completed in a timely manner.
 Provides technical guidance on the appropriate application and interpretation of statistical analyses, sampling plans, engineering studies, and quality data.
 Ensures appropriate execution of risk management activities and application of tools such as FMEA, FTA, PHA, and other applicable risk analysis methodologies.
 Maintains a thorough understanding of internal Quality Management System procedures and ensures the team operates in compliance with applicable processes and requirements.
 Product & Consumer Quality 
 Ensures product knowledge, foreseeable consumer use, and play patterns are incorporated into Quality Engineering decisions and product risk assessments.
 Utilizes quality system data, consumer feedback, testing results, product returns, manufacturing performance, and post-market information to understand product and process performance.
 Identifies opportunities to improve product quality, reliability, durability, and consumer satisfaction based on available data and lessons learned.
 Leads or supports investigation and resolution of significant post-market product quality and safety issues within assigned areas.
 Partners with cross-functional teams to ensure lessons learned from consumer and field performance are incorporated into current and future product development.
 Culture & Continuous Improvement 
 Fosters a culture of quality, consumer safety, accountability, continuous learning, and shared ownership within the team and across cross-functional partnerships.
 Identifies and leads continuous improvement initiatives within assigned areas through the appropriate application of continuous improvement methodologies and tools.
 Assesses Quality Engineering processes and identifies opportunities to improve effectiveness, consistency, scalability, and efficiency.
 Leads cross-functional improvement efforts and ensures improvements maintain compliance with regulatory requirements, standards, and internal Quality Management System requirements.
 Uses KPIs, quality metrics, lessons learned, and benchmarking to identify opportunities for improvement.
 Promotes adoption and sharing of best practices across Quality Engineering teams.
 Builds business cases, as appropriate, for significant improvement opportunities and communicates the expected quality, operational, consumer, and business impact.
What We’re Looking For: 
 Exceptional interpersonal and people leadership skills with demonstrated ability to lead, coach, develop, and motivate technical professionals.
 Demonstrated knowledge of consumer product regulatory standards, with an emphasis on toys or children's products.
 Strong technical judgment with the ability to evaluate complex product quality, safety, regulatory, manufacturing, and consumer issues and make sound risk-based decisions.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to use data to identify solutions and drive effective actions.
 Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and leaders without direct authority.
 Ability to balance product safety, compliance, quality, consumer experience, business needs, cost, and schedule while maintaining appropriate quality standards.
 Demonstrated ability to effectively manage multiple projects, team priorities, and resources without missing critical deadlines.
 High level of personal and professional integrity and trustworthiness with a strong work ethic, sound judgment, and accountability.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including listening and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly and concisely.
 Resourceful, diplomatic, and professional, with the ability to build strong relationships across functions, geographies, and organizational levels.
 Collaborative leader with strong results orientation, positive attitude, and demonstrated ability to create accountability while maintaining effective working relationships.
 Demonstrated ability to develop others through coaching, feedback, technical mentoring, and meaningful development opportunities.
 Adaptable; able to shift priorities and focus as departmental, product development, and business demands change.
 Experience, Education, & Skills: 
 Bachelor's degree in Industrial, Electrical, Mechanical, Materials Engineering, or related technical discipline.
 6+ years of progressive experience in product development, product engineering, manufacturing, or quality roles, preferably within toys, children's products, or consumer products.
 Previous experience leading engineers, technical teams, or significant cross-functional programs; formal people-management experience preferred.
 Working knowledge of global toy and consumer product safety standards and regulatory requirements.
 Strong knowledge of Quality Management System structure, procedures, and implementation.
 Experience with product development processes from concept through production and post-market support.
 Knowledge of risk management principles and tools such as FMEA, FTA, PHA, and other structured risk assessment methodologies.
 Knowledge of engineering and quality tools including statistical analysis, Cause-and-Effect Analysis, root cause analysis, process mapping, sampling methodologies, and engineering studies.
 Experience interpreting quality and product performance data and applying statistical analysis to support engineering decisions.
 Experience working with internal and/or third-party product testing laboratories.
 Experience supporting global manufacturing, suppliers, and product development organizations.
 Knowledge of Human Factors/Usability Engineering principles and their application to toys and consumer products preferred.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office, project management tools, and statistical analysis software such as Minitab.

 We hold strong opinions loosely — bring conviction, stay open to being wrong.

 Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’EDC ! 
 À EDC, nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Nous leur offrons les outils financiers et l’expertise dont elles ont besoin pour explorer de nouveaux marchés et réduire les risques, dans un seul but : bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce. 
 Poste : Analyste des risques ou analyste principale des risques/analyste principal des risques, Évaluation des risques et gestion du portefeuille, niveaux  17 à 19 
 Type d’emploi : Affectation permanente/ contractuelle
 Détails de la rémunération : 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 17 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 84 698 $ à 112 931 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 18 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 96 557 $ à 128 743 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 19 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 112 006 $ à 149 341 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Veuillez noter que la rémunération au rendement ne s’applique qu’aux postes permanents. 
 Lieu de travail 
 Exportation et développement Canada évolue dans un environnement de travail hybride, avec une exigence actuelle de présence au bureau de deux jours par semaine, laquelle passera à trois jours par semaine à compter de septembre 2026 (sous réserve de modifications) .
 La personne choisie peut travailler à partir du siège social d’EDC à Ottawa ou à partir du Carrefour communautaire à Toronto, ou à Montréal.
 Une aide à la réinstallation est offerte aux candidats et candidates admissibles ( ne s’applique qu’aux postes permanents. )
 Candidats internes, veuillez consulter la page Service Now intitulée « Mouvements internes - ce que vous devez savoir ». 
 À propos d’EDC 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. En tant que société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer.
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce.
 Conciliation travail-vie personnelle : EDC offre un régime concurrentiel en ce qui concerne la rémunération et la conciliation travail-vie personnelle : différentes options de travail hybride, trois à quatre semaines de vacances, une période de fermeture, des vendredis d’été raccourcis et les vendredis sans réunion.
 Perfectionnement professionnel : Profitez de nos occasions d’apprentissage continu, notamment des programmes de formation, des ateliers et de la formation linguistique.
 Culture inclusive : Intégrez un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif qui lutte pour l’équité en matière d’emploi et valorise la diversité des idées, des forces et des origines pour favoriser la réussite.
 Programmes de bien-être : Nous offrons des initiatives de bien-être, de l’aide à la santé mentale et des programmes de conditionnement physique pour veiller à votre santé et à votre bonheur.
 Investissement dans la collectivité : Participez à des activités de bénévolat et donnez au suivant grâce à un éventail de programmes de responsabilité sociale.
 Aperçu de l’équipe : 
 L’Équipe de l’évaluation des risques et de la gestion du portefeuille surveille le portefeuille d’assurances en procédant à une évaluation des risques de crédit et à la gestion du portefeuille de façon indépendante, tout en veillant à ce que les mesures appropriées soient prises lorsque le risque de crédit d’une entreprise n’est plus jugé acceptable. Elle participe également à l’examen continu des normes d’octroi et de vérification du crédit et des politiques et procédures en matière d’acceptation des risques du Groupe des assurances. 
 L’Équipe est à la recherche de professionnels du crédit dynamiques et motivés pour gérer un portefeuille d’acheteurs en évaluant les risques de crédit et les risques financiers de façon indépendante afin de déterminer l’acceptation du risque commercial et les capacités de remboursement de ces entreprises, en appui au programme d’assurance d’EDC. 
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 Procéder à des contrôles préalables et aux analyses nécessaires afin d’évaluer la solvabilité et le niveau de risque d’un acheteur ou d’une transaction selon la situation financière en question et d’autres facteurs comme la conjoncture économique du pays et les modalités de paiement.  
 Évaluer les nouvelles demandes de crédit. 
 Assurer une surveillance adéquate et un suivi rapide du portefeuille d’acheteurs pour veiller à ce que les dossiers soient à jour et réduire au minimum les délais relatifs à l’octroi de crédit. 
 Analyser et commenter les développements entourant les secteurs, les marchés et les portefeuilles. 
 Observer en tout temps les normes de crédit reconnues pour disposer des documents nécessaires, mener de bonnes analyses de crédit, et recommander les décisions appropriées. 
 Préparer les évaluations de crédit et présenter des recommandations aux approbateurs de crédit disposant de l’autorité appropriée. 
 Transmettre activement son savoir sectoriel et industriel pour soutenir les équipes sectorielles, les partenaires internes et les clients. 
 S’informer sur les pratiques générales en matière de souscription en assurance crédit. 
 Veiller au respect des règles entourant l’intégrité des données. 
 Assurer la liaison avec les acheteurs, les banques, les fournisseurs d’information et d’autres entités afin d’évaluer les questions relatives au crédit. 
 Apporter continuellement de nouvelles idées d’amélioration pour EDC en travaillant en étroite collaboration avec ses collègues, avec les clients et avec les principaux intermédiaires. Contribuer aux projets ponctuels liés au processus et à d’autres améliorations. 
 Analyste principale des risques ou analyste principal des risques (Gestion des risques de portefeuille 19) – autres responsabilités 
 Posséder une connaissance vaste et approfondie des questions de crédit dans les secteurs concernés et formuler des recommandations en temps utile pour atténuer les risques. 
 Diriger de façon proactive tous les aspects de la gestion du portefeuille, y compris la collecte, l’analyse et la communication efficace des données, ce qui comprend la présentation d’information aux parties prenantes et aux comités pertinents.​ 
 Cultiver un réseau de parties prenantes, en interne et à l’extérieur de la Société, dans l’optique d’améliorer la gestion du portefeuille, s’il y a lieu, de manière à assurer la réussite des projets.

You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter.
 Please read carefully: 
 1. Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What do you do for fun?
 3. Show us what you’ve done.
 Please include links to social accounts, campaigns, posts, videos, or other work you’ve helped create or manage.
 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.
 4. Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 We’re looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly and you can expect a prompt response.

Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

 Lead one of Canada’s largest aluminum smelters and shape its strategic direction for the future. Through inclusive and unifying leadership, you will build on ABI’s strengths, align the organization around a shared vision, and position the operation for sustained, long-term performance.
 About the role 
 Reporting to the Vice-President of Operations, North America, you will:
 Lead site-wide EHS strategy, ensuring effective systems, resources and accountability to manage critical risks and uphold legal and environmental requirements. Develop leaders, support employees in raising concerns and stopping unsafe work, turn learning into continuous improvement and embed safety as a core value.
 Set and execute the site’s mid- to long-term strategy, aligning resources and priorities with Alcoa’s direction and values.

 Experience developing leaders’ safety capability, responding to workforce concerns and supporting speak-up and stop-work; evidence of translating incident and audit learning into stronger work practices and controls.

 About the role 
 Our Canada Architecture team works on Salesforce’s largest and most complex customers across Canada’s many industries. We don’t stop at showing customers what’s possible; we prove it by building it with them. Success here is a working prototype or a deployed asset, not a great deck.

 You’ll sit within the Canada architecture team and belong to the broader Regulated Industries & Canada architecture community.  Lead agentic AI architecture on strategic accounts. Serve as the aligned architect for your accounts.  Architecture-sourced pipeline and measurable progression on priority opportunities in your accounts.

Lieu de travail : Saint-Hyacinthe, QC (sur site) 
 Statut : Permanent, temps plein 
 L'aventure Foxtrot Industriel 
 Projet né à l'Université de Sherbrooke entre 2018 et 2020 par ses fondateurs ingénieurs Benoît Serrano-Parent et Charles-Éric Raymond, l'entreprise a rapidement démontré l'efficacité de ses prototypes sur le terrain avant de conclure une première transaction majeure auprès d’une entreprise renommée. 
 Aujourd'hui basée à Saint-Hyacinthe, Foxtrot conçoit et fabrique au Québec des robots mobiles et chariots motorisés télécommandés sans fil (gammes TANGO, SOLO 10/20/60 et OMNI). Ces équipements permettent de déplacer des charges colossales de 20 à 60 tonnes dans des espaces industriels extrêmement restreints sans recourir aux grues ni aux ponts roulants. Nos solutions font économiser du temps, de l'espace et de la main-d'œuvre tout en éliminant les risques d'accident. 
 Notre culture repose sur trois valeurs fondamentales : l'action (faire avancer les choses sur le terrain), l'innovation (dans les produits et procédés) et l'engagement envers les besoins réels des clients. 
 Le contexte: En pleine phase d'industrialisation pour doubler notre production par mois, Foxtrot cherche un esprit pratique pour optimiser la chaîne d'assemblage et la fabrication. Rattaché directement aux opérations, vous serez le pont entre la conception 3D, le plancher de montage et nos partenaires sous-traitants. 
 Vos responsabilités au quotidien 
 Revoir l'aménagement des postes de travail ( layout ) pour rationaliser le flux de montage des robots. 
 Concevoir des gabarits et outils facilitant le travail quotidien des électromécaniciens et assembleurs. 
 Analyser les pièces métalliques et sous-ensembles pour déterminer s'il est préférable de les fabriquer en interne ou de les confier à des sous-traitants. 
 Identifier des partenaires sous-traitants (usinage, découpe laser, peinture, soudure), évaluer leurs coûts et leur fournir la documentation technique complète. 
 Produire et mettre à jour les dessins de fabrication 3D et rédiger les instructions d'assemblage. 
 Le profil recherché 
 Baccalauréat en génie mécanique ou pertinent (ou formation technique / DEC équivalent). 
 Bonne compréhension des procédés de transformation métallique (découpe de métal, usinage, peinture, soudure). 
 Maîtrise des logiciels de modélisation 3D et lecture de plans. 
 Connaissance des concepts d'amélioration continue et d'optimisation des procédés manufacturiers. 
 Français et anglais fonctionnel (compréhension écrite et orale des documents techniques). 
 Esprit d'équipe, présence sur le terrain et créativité pour résoudre des problèmes mécaniques concrets. 
 Vos avantages et conditions de travail 
 Horaire flexible favorisant la conciliation travail-vie personnelle. 
 Programme d'assurances collectives. 
 Vacances. 
 Opportunité de jouer un rôle clé dans une entreprise technologique québécoise en forte croissance. 
 Ambiance conviviale, responsabilités évolutives et activités sociales sont au rendez-vous.

About 1Password

Device Infrastructure Services owns the full lifecycle of hardware and operating systems across 1Password. The team is looking for the Staff Engineer who will lead its next chapter: a deliberate shift from legacy device management patterns towards devops and AI-enabled operations.

You'll be the technical leader of this team, responsible for setting the roadmap for this transformation and making sure it gets executed. This isn't a role where you hand off a roadmap and step back: you'll be in the build alongside the team, coaching engineers and raising the ceiling on what they're capable of. If you're excited by building scalable systems, shaping the strategy behind tools the whole company depends on, and bringing out the best work in the people around you, we want to hear from you.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

What we're looking for:

 - 7+ years of IT and enterprise endpoint management experience, including 2+ years at a senior or staff IC level, with a track record of building and managing endpoints with Gitops practices.

 - Demonstrate broad knowledge of enterprise endpoint management, deep operating system-level experience, and the ability to recognize patterns across a fleet and build fixes that prevent recurrence.

 - Practical experience using AI tools to enable or accelerate IT operations and the judgment to know where AI speeds things up versus where it introduces risk.

 - Proven ability to define and drive technical roadmaps, seeing around corners and balancing long-term vision with near-term execution.

 -  Strong scripting and IaC ability (Bash, Python, and Terraform at minimum) — both writing production-quality automation yourself and reviewing others' code with a critical eye.

 -  Deep working knowledge of enterprise security fundamentals as they apply to endpoints: encryption, patch/vulnerability management, EDR, least-privilege enforcement, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar).

 - Lead through change, collaborate effectively, and mentor engineers while maintaining a focused and impactful team environment.

What you can expect:

 - Own the technical direction of our Device Infrastructure Services, the tooling and standards that keep ~2,000 endpoints compliant, configured, and secure.

 - Drive the technical direction of a DevOps operating model for the fleet — config-as-code, version control, code review, and CI/CD pipelines in place of manual console changes — and drive adoption of that model across the IT team.

 -  Lead the adoption of responsible agentic AI across the device team, building the guardrails that decide what agents can act on autonomously and what still needs a human checkpoint.

 -  Act as the final escalation point for high-severity endpoint incidents, including deep machine-level diagnosis on both macOS and Windows hardware.

 - Partner across IT, Security, and product teams building custom solutions and helping push their initiatives across the finish line.

 - Assess and pilot new tooling (e.g., MDM platform migrations, patch management systems) and drive build-vs-buy decisions.
